title: Third rule — common Roman consensus as Apostolic tradition; Lenten fast example
source_text: XVIII. Tertia denique regula eorum est, Quod illud, quod Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae communi consensu docent, ex Apostolica traditione descendere revera pro traditione Apostolica habendum sit: licet tale sit ut ab Ecclesia potuerit institui. Cujusmodi traditionem volunt esse jejunium illud quod vocant Quadragesimale.
pass_a_gloss: Finally their third rule is this: that what the doctors of the Roman Church teach by common consent to descend from Apostolic tradition is truly to be held as an Apostolic tradition — even if it is of such a kind that the Church could have instituted it. Of this sort they want that fast to be which they call the Quadragesimal (Lenten) fast.
pass_b_english: Third rule: whatever Roman doctors by common consent say descends from Apostolic tradition is to be treated as Apostolic — even when the Church herself could have set it up.
They class the Quadragesimal (Lenten) fast under this head.

lemmas.gloss: that fast which they call Quadragesimal / Lenten

choices.why: Same Lent example already named under Apostolic traditions in XIII.

choices.term: licet tale sit ut ab Ecclesia potuerit institui
choices.english: even if the Church could have instituted it
choices.why: Widens Apostolic claim beyond only-God rites.
